newsitem.title: USA: Weakness in U.S. stocks continues in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Weakness in U.S. stocks continues in late trading.

text.p: Wall Street stocks continued to show overall softness in late trading Wednesday after two key technology companies forecast disapointing earnings.

The Dow Jones industrial average was off 35, or about a half a percent, to 7725. The index slumped over sixty points after the opening of trading but some morning buying stemmed the loss, halving the losses. But the index fell back again and has been trading steadily lower through the afternoon.
The Nasdaq Composite was off nearly ten points to 1433.
Big Board volume was relatively light, with roughly 363 million shares traded and about 90 minutes of trading left.
The weakness came after profit warnings from Seagate Technology Inc and Gateway 2000 Inc raised concerns that the tech sector may face greater difficulties in the weeks ahead, analysts said.
Adding to the Dow's weakness was Eastman Kodak, down 2-4/8 to 77-3/4, Philip Morris Cos Inc, off 1-5/8 to 45-1/8 and Procter & Gamble Co, losing 1-1/8 to 138-1/2.
Bonds were strong. The 30-year U.S. treasury bond was up 15/32 with a 6.69 percent yield.
